concurrencyBound.rationale: AFC-22 names 'bounded concurrency' explicitly but gives no number. 8 is chosen with margin below the 10-concurrent-subprocess point already measured safe on this codebase's own tooling (keryx-shell-stress.ts T2), leaving headroom for the rest of an agent turn's own concurrent work rather than saturating it.

worstCaseCeiling.note: 2.14 spawns/page is TODAY's measured per-page linear cost (T10 inventory + this task's own re-measurement), used here only as a non-regression floor: a degenerate, no-shared-base-revision corpus must not spawn MORE than the unbatched baseline already does. It is not the target — it is the worst case the target must never exceed.

gitSubprocessBudget.rationale: AFC-22's named mechanism is 'checks groups of equal base revisions in batches' (wiki-specification.md:88). Once implemented, cost should scale with the number of DISTINCT VerifiedAt revisions a run touches, not the page count: one existence probe, one batched `git log`, one batched `git diff` per shared base revision, each pathspec-scoped to every page sharing that base. Real corpora cluster (a `wiki refresh` run stamps a whole batch of pages at one HEAD), so distinct-revision count is expected to stay far below page count in practice; this profile does not assume a specific cluster size, only the batching principle plus a floor that guarantees the pathological case is never worse than the status quo.

hardCeiling.anchoredOn: 10% of DEFAULT_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS (120000ms), this codebase's own existing ceiling for a single interactive tool call (src/harness/tool/builtin/shell-exec-tool.ts:46) — wiki_freshness is one call among several an agent turn may make, so it must not itself consume more than a modest slice of the budget any single tool call is already allowed.

latencyBudgetMs.rationale: `perScale` assumes typical base-revision clustering (a run touching at most a few dozen distinct base revisions, not one per page) and converts the git-subprocess budget above into wall-clock using this repo's own measured per-subprocess overhead (~26ms, from this task's real-git measurement: see the benchmark's own logged run) purely as a unit-conversion constant. `repeated` is far cheaper than `cold` because AFC-22 requires an in-run cache: a second read of a decision already produced in this run must reuse it rather than re-spawning git. `hardCeiling` is the single number this profile is willing to call a hard requirement independent of any assumption about corpus shape; `perScale` is a target, not yet a gate.

cachePolicy.inRunCache: Authorized and expected by AFC-22 ('caches Git results within a run'): a process-lifetime memo keyed by (base revision, pathspec-set or individual path) so a 'repeated' call inside one run/process pays for each (revision, path) git fact at most once. Not implemented by this task — this is the target the code half of a later lane (L8's batching/caching change, sequenced after L1) is checked against.
cachePolicy.persistentCache: NOT authorized by this profile. wiki-specification.md:88 requires a separately measured basis before a cache surviving process exit is introduced, and no such measurement exists yet. A future profile version may authorize one, but only after it exists as its own measured proposal, not as a side effect of this task.
cachePolicy.dirtyCheckoutHandling: AFC-22 requires batching/caching to account for a dirty or untracked working tree. Not implemented by this task. `fixtures/wiki-freshness-scale/manifest.json` reserves a `dirtyCheckout` corpus variant so a later implementation has something to test against; this profile does not yet set a separate budget number for it.

rankingWeights.formula: two-key stable sort, no weighted scoring formula
rankingWeights.note: This is a RECORD of `src/wiki/freshness/report.ts`'s existing `entries.sort` (AC13), not a new design — read here, not written. M09 asks for ranking weights to live in the versioned calibration profile alongside the latency budget; today's ranking has no weighted formula to record beyond this fixed ordering. If a future task introduces weighted ranking (e.g. blending confidence, category severity or recency), it must bump `profileVersion` and record the new weights here BEFORE the ranking code changes, mirroring AC-22's own 'budget agreed before optimisation' ordering.

gitFailureContract.requirement: AC-22 clause 2 / AC-W05 clause 3: a git failure yields unknown, distinguishable from the ordinary 'never verified' unknown.
gitFailureContract.closedBy: flow 236 T7 — src/sync/provenance.ts's `gitCmdResult`, src/wiki/freshness/page-freshness.ts's `gitFailure` field and src/wiki/freshness/report.ts's `not-a-git-repository` / `git-command-failed` limitation codes. This profile's benchmark re-verifies the contract holds at 50/500/2000 pages; it does not re-implement or re-derive it.

outOfScope: The batching-by-base-revision code change itself (src/wiki/freshness/page-freshness.ts) — this profile is the precondition for that change, not the change.
A persistent (cross-process) cache — not authorized at all by this profile.
A dirty/untracked-checkout cost budget number — the fixture variant is reserved but not measured or budgeted here.
A weighted ranking formula — only today's unweighted two-key sort is recorded.
Any change to src/wiki/freshness/**, src/sync/provenance.ts, src/ctx/**, src/commands/ctx.ts, package.json or a retention module — all sibling-owned in this flow.
